items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I worked with Stan in different venues, concert situations, but never to tour

ctx.x: No. Those things are great. And that’s what — people I don’t think have a realistic picture of what jazz musicians, or a lot of musicians, how they really make a living. That playing with Ella and the list of people you’ve played with, Zoot Sims and Sweets Edison, those are great moments, and you’re recording here, but that doesn’t happen every single day.

No. Those are the highlights and high points. But unless you maybe were touring for long periods with a Stan Getz, or — like for instance I worked with Stan in different venues, concert situations, but never to tour, for like six months or whatever. So yeah, you have to fill up the rest of your time with other stuff, and so I’ve done a lot of stuff. I said to somebody recently, I’ve done just about everything except maybe play in a circus band, because they didn’t use keyboards then, now they do. But a lot of it…

Well you said a couple of minutes ago you were talking about the studio music and you said most of it was just craft. And at first I thought you were going to say crap. But I think it’s a telling thing that you didn’t say that, because even playing on a Rice-a-Roni commercial, you have to do what’s required, and not more. Because I’ve heard plenty of players who can play the piano like crazy but they don’t understand the gig — if it’s solo piano if it’s in a restaurant or something.
